title: Expanding Kadi On Your Own: Save/Load, Drag & Drop, Tournament & LAN Multiplayer
summary: Learn how to independently upgrade Kadi with persistent JSON save files (`user://`), interactive drag-and-drop card physics, 2D foil shaders, a 100-point Kenyan Tournament Elimination mode, and LAN multiplayer (`@rpc`).
learningObjectives: Serialize and load player stats, win streaks, and Kadi Coins to user://kadi_profile.json using FileAccess and JSON
Implement smooth mouse/touch drag-and-drop card play with _gui_input() and 2D holographic foil shaders
Build a Main Menu scene transition and official Kenyan 100-point Tournament Elimination scoring
Architect Pass-and-Play privacy shields and 4-player LAN multiplayer using ENetMultiplayerPeer and @rpc
tangibleGoal: Drag cards across the table onto the discard pile, watch your win streak and Kadi Coins persist across restarts, score 100-point tournament rounds, and sync moves over LAN!

lessons.title: Persistent Player Profiles, Win Streaks & Coins (`FileAccess`, `JSON` & `user://`)
lessons.tangibleOutcome: Press **F5**, win a Kadi match, close the game window, and press **F5** again — your **Wins, Current Streak, and Kadi Coins** are loaded automatically from disk!
lessons.beyondKadi:
Every commercial game needs persistent save data:
- **2D Platformer**: Saving unlocked levels, best speedrun times, and collected stars.
- **RPG / Roguelike**: Saving character level, gold, equipped weapon IDs, and permanent meta-upgrades.
- **Rule #1 of Godot Saving**: Always write to `user://` (the OS-writable app data folder), **never** `res://` (which becomes read-only inside an exported `.exe` or `.apk`!).
lessons.transferChallenge: **Your Solo Task**: Add a `"high_score_streak": 0` key to `SaveManager.profile`. Whenever `profile["streak"] > profile["high_score_streak"]`, update `profile["high_score_streak"] = profile["streak"]` before calling `save_profile()`, and display the all-time best streak on `Table.tscn`!
editorSteps: In Godot's **FileSystem dock**, right-click `res://scripts/` -> **New -> Script**, name it `save_manager.gd`, and click **Create**.
Go to **Project -> Project Settings -> Globals -> Autoload**, select `res://scripts/save_manager.gd`, set **Node Name** to `SaveManager`, and click **Add**.
Paste the `save_manager.gd` script below and press **Ctrl+S**.
In `table.gd`, call `SaveManager.record_match_result(player == 0)` inside `_execute_move()` when a winner is detected, and display `SaveManager.get_summary_text()` in `status_label`.
verificationSteps: Press **F5** and check the top HUD or Output console to verify `Wins: 0 | Streak: 0 | Coins: 100` loads cleanly even before any save file exists on disk.
In Godot's top menu, click **Project -> Open User Data Folder** to see the real folder on your computer where `kadi_profile.json` is stored!
troubleshootingTips: **Save works in Editor but fails in exported `.exe` / `.apk`**: Verify your path starts with `user://` (`"user://kadi_profile.json"`), NOT `res://`!

**`Invalid get index 'wins' (on base: 'Nil')` when loading**: Always guard `JSON.parse_string()` with `if parsed is Dictionary:` and use `.merge(parsed, true)` so missing keys keep their safe defaults.
keyTakeaways: `res://` is read-only in exported games; `user://` is guaranteed writable on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, and Web.
`JSON.stringify(dict, "\t")` converts a GDScript `Dictionary` into human-readable JSON text; `JSON.parse_string(text)` parses it back.
Using `profile.merge(parsed, true)` safely upgrades older save files when you add new keys in future game updates!
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
# Saving Player Progress to Disk (`FileAccess` & `JSON`)

> [!TIP]
> **Tangible Milestone:** Right now, closing the game window wipes your memory clean. In this lesson, you will build a reusable `SaveManager` Autoload singleton that saves **Matches Played, Wins, Win Streak, and Kadi Coins** to `user://kadi_profile.json`!

When you improve Kadi on your own — or build a new RPG, platformer, or roguelike — players expect their achievements, unlocked card backs, and settings to persist between sessions.

## 1. Why `user://` Instead of `res://`?

In Godot 4.3, there are two virtual filesystem prefixes:

| Path Prefix | Where It Points | Can You Write to It at Runtime? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`res://`** | Your project source assets (`scenes/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`) | **NO** — Packaged inside a read-only `.pck` archive when exported! |
| **`user://`** | OS-specific writable app folder (`%APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/...` on Windows, internal app storage on Android) | **YES** — Always writable for save files, profiles, and settings! |

## 2. The 3-Step JSON Save/Load Pattern

1. **Keep state in a default `Dictionary`** (`var profile: Dictionary = {"wins": 0, "matches": 0, "streak": 0, "coins": 100}`).
2. **To Save**: Open `"user://kadi_profile.json"` with `[[FileAccess]].open(SAVE_PATH, FileAccess.WRITE)` and call `file.store_string([[JSON]].stringify(profile, "	"))`.
3. **To Load**: Check `if FileAccess.file_exists(SAVE_PATH):`, read the text with `FileAccess.get_file_as_string(SAVE_PATH)`, parse it with `JSON.parse_string(text)`, and merge it into `profile` using `profile.merge(parsed, true)`.

## Line-by-Line Code Walkthrough

| Line | GDScript Code | Exact Meaning & Why It's Written This Way |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Line 4** | `const SAVE_PATH: String = "user://kadi_profile.json"` | Stores the save file in Godot's writable `user://` directory. |
| **Line 15** | `var file := FileAccess.open(SAVE_PATH, FileAccess.WRITE)` | Opens (or creates) `kadi_profile.json` for writing. |
| **Line 17** | `file.store_string(JSON.stringify(profile, "	"))` | Serializes the `profile` dictionary as pretty-printed JSON. |
| **Line 20** | `if not FileAccess.file_exists(SAVE_PATH): return` | Safely exits on first launch when no save file exists yet. |
| **Line 23** | `if parsed is Dictionary: profile.merge(parsed, true)` | Overwrites default keys with saved values while preserving any newly added default keys! |

quizQuestions.prompt: Why must runtime save files in Godot 4.3 use the `user://` prefix instead of `res://`?
choices: Because `res://` becomes read-only inside the packaged `.pck` archive once you export your game to Windows, Android, or Web
Because `FileAccess` syntax only accepts strings of 7 characters or fewer
Because `res://` automatically deletes JSON files when `_ready()` finishes
Because `JSON.stringify()` cannot format dictionaries stored in `res://`
quizQuestions.explanation: When exported, `res://` is packed inside a read-only resource bundle, whereas `user://` points to a dedicated OS-writable application data directory.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does `profile.merge(parsed, true)` do when loading a saved `Dictionary` from disk?
choices: It updates keys present in `parsed` while keeping default values for any new keys added in later versions of your game
It deletes all keys in `profile` that have integer values
It encrypts the JSON string with a password
It converts the Dictionary into a PackedScene
quizQuestions.explanation: `Dictionary.merge(other, true)` overwrites matching keys with saved values while preserving any new default keys that didn't exist when the older save file was created.

lessons.bodyMarkdown:
# Main Menu, Scene Transitions & Kenyan 100-Point Tournament Scoring

> [!TIP]
> **Tangible Milestone:** Add a real **Kenyan Tournament Elimination Mode** where holding a Joker or 3 when someone else wins costs you `50` or `30` penalty points—and upgrade your AI to prioritize shedding high-risk cards!

## 1. Kenyan Kadi Tournament Point Values

In competitive Kenyan Kadi tournaments, hoarding Penalty cards (`Joker`, `3`, `2`) and `Ace`s is risky: if another player goes out first, every card still trapped in your hand adds penalty points toward the **100-point elimination cap**:

| Card in Hand at Round End | Tournament Penalty Points | Strategic Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Joker (`15`)** | **50 points** | Holding 2 Jokers when someone wins eliminates you immediately (`100 pts`)! |
| **3 (`THREE`)** | **30 points** | High risk to hold late in a round. |
| **2 (`TWO`) or Ace (`ACE`)** | **20 points** | Valuable blockers, but expensive if caught holding them. |
| **Jack (`11`), Queen (`12`), King (`13`)** | **10 points** | Moderate penalty. |
| **Number Cards (`4..10`)** | **Face value (`4..10` pts)** | Lowest penalty risk. |

## 2. Switching Scenes with `SceneTree.change_scene_to_file()`

When your game has a `MainMenu.tscn` and a `Table.tscn`, you switch between them with one call on `[[SceneTree]]`:

```gdscript
get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://scenes/table/table.tscn")
```

Because `GameState`, `TurnManager`, and `SaveManager` are **Autoload singletons**, they live directly under `root` above the active scene and preserve all settings across scene changes!

codeSnippets.code:
# File: res://scripts/tournament_rules.gd
class_name TournamentRules
extends RefCounted

const ELIMINATION_POINTS: int = 100

static func card_points(card: CardData) -> int:
	if card == null:
		return 0
	match card.rank:
		CardTypes.Ranks.JOKER: return 50
		CardTypes.Ranks.THREE: return 30
		CardTypes.Ranks.TWO, CardTypes.Ranks.ACE: return 20
		CardTypes.Ranks.JACK, CardTypes.Ranks.QUEEN, CardTypes.Ranks.KING: return 10
		_: return card.rank

static func compute_hand_points(hand: Array) -> int:
	var total: int = 0
	for c in hand:
		total += card_points(c)
	return total

## Heuristic scorer so smart AI sheds high-risk cards while saving 1 Ace for defense:
static func score_ai_move(cards: Array, penalty_stack: int, hand_size: int) -> int:
	if cards.is_empty():
		return -999
	var score: int = 0
	for c in cards:
		score += card_points(c)
		if c.rank == CardTypes.Ranks.ACE and penalty_stack == 0 and hand_size > 2:
			score -= 35 # Save Ace for emergency penalty defense!
	return score
codeSnippets.caption: Kenyan Kadi tournament point calculator & smart AI heuristic (`res://scripts/tournament_rules.gd`).

lessons.title: Pass-and-Play Hotseat & LAN Multiplayer (`ENetMultiplayerPeer` & `@rpc`)
lessons.tangibleOutcome: Play Kadi with friends either on one device via a **Pass-and-Play Privacy Curtain** or across laptops/phones over Wi-Fi using Godot 4.3's **`ENetMultiplayerPeer` and `@rpc`**!
lessons.beyondKadi:
Godot 4.3's high-level multiplayer (`ENetMultiplayerPeer` + `@rpc` + `MultiplayerSpawner`) works identically across genres:
- **Co-op Action RPG**: Syncing player positions and spell casts across Wi-Fi.
- **Turn-Based Strategy / Board Game**: Syncing turn actions cleanly with `@rpc("any_peer", "call_local", "reliable")`.
lessons.transferChallenge: **Your Solo Task**: Add a quick-chat emoji bar (`"🔥 Moto!"`, `"😂 Pole!"`, `"📢 Niko Kadi!"`) that calls an `@rpc("any_peer", "call_local", "reliable") func send_table_emote(sender_name: String, message: String)` so players can react live across the network!

editorSteps: For **Local Pass-and-Play**, add a full-screen `ColorRect` under `HUD` named `PassDeviceOverlay` with a centered `ReadyButton` (`"Pass phone to Player X — Tap when ready"`).
For **LAN Wi-Fi Multiplayer**, use `ENetMultiplayerPeer.new()` to host (`create_server(8910, 4)`) or join (`create_client(ip, 8910)`).
Decorate state-syncing methods with `@rpc("any_peer", "call_local", "reliable")` and invoke them with `.rpc(...)`.
verificationSteps: In Godot 4.3's top menu, click **Debug -> Customize Run Instances**, check **Enable Multiple Instances**, set count to **2**, and press **F5** to launch two game windows side-by-side on your computer and test LAN hosting & joining!
troubleshootingTips: **`@rpc` runs on remote peers but not on the sender**: Add `"call_local"` inside `@rpc("any_peer", "call_local", "reliable")` so the function executes on both the caller and all connected peers!
keyTakeaways: `@rpc("any_peer", "call_local", "reliable")` is the golden combination for turn-based card and strategy games: any player can submit their turn, it runs locally and remotely, and TCP-like reliability guarantees no dropped card plays.
**Debug -> Customize Run Instances** in Godot 4.3 lets you test 2–4 multiplayer windows on a single machine!
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
# Local Pass-and-Play & LAN Multiplayer (`ENetMultiplayerPeer` & `@rpc`)

> [!TIP]
> **Tangible Milestone:** Turn your single-player vs. AI Kadi game into a **Multiplayer Party Game** — supporting both **1-Phone Pass-and-Play Hotseat** and **Multi-Device Wi-Fi LAN Multiplayer**!

## 1. Local Pass-and-Play Hotseat (The Privacy Curtain Pattern)

When 2–4 human friends share one phone or laptop, you don't want Seat 1 to see Seat 2's cards during the handoff!
1. Whenever `TurnManager.turn_changed` fires for a human seat, hide `player_hand_container.visible = false` and show `pass_device_overlay.visible = true` (`"Pass device to Player 2 — Tap to Reveal Hand"`).
2. When the next player taps `ReadyButton`, hide `pass_device_overlay` and rebuild `player_hand_container` from `GameState.hands[current_seat]`!

## 2. Wi-Fi / LAN Multiplayer in 15 Lines with `@rpc`

Godot 4.3 has a built-in high-level networking API (`ENetMultiplayerPeer`) and `@rpc` (Remote Procedure Call) annotations:

| `@rpc` Argument | What It Means |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`"any_peer"`** | Allows non-host client players (Seats 1, 2, 3) to invoke this RPC when they play a card. |
| **`"call_local"`** | Runs the function on the sender's machine as well as all connected peers so state stays 100% identical. |
| **`"reliable"`** | Guarantees every card play packet arrives in order (essential for turn-based games!). |

codeSnippets.caption: Godot 4.3 LAN host/join and `@rpc` move synchronization.

practicePrompt.instructions: Write an `@rpc("any_peer", "call_local", "reliable")` function `func sync_niko_kadi(seat: int) -> void` that sets `GameState.announced_kadi[seat] = true`.
practicePrompt.hint: Place `@rpc("any_peer", "call_local", "reliable")` right above `func sync_niko_kadi(seat: int) -> void:`.
practicePrompt.starterCode: # Synchronize Niko Kadi announcement across all peers:
practicePrompt.expectedOutput: Syncs the player's Niko Kadi announcement across all connected LAN devices.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why do we include `"call_local"` inside `@rpc("any_peer", "call_local", "reliable")` when syncing a turn-based move?
choices: So calling `func_name.rpc(...)` executes the function on the sender's own game instance as well as on all remote peers
So the game only runs without Wi-Fi
So textures compress faster
So `HBoxContainer` centers cards vertically
quizQuestions.explanation: Without `"call_local"`, `.rpc()` only executes on remote peers; adding `"call_local"` runs the exact same state update on both the local sender and remote peers.

debugChallenge.bugDescription: Saving works inside the Godot Editor, but as soon as you export the game to Windows `.exe` or Android `.apk`, `FileAccess.open()` returns `null` and player progress is never saved! Tap the buggy line.
debugChallenge.explanation: In exported builds, `res://` is packed inside a read-only archive (`.pck` or `.apk`), so `FileAccess.open("res://...", FileAccess.WRITE)` fails and returns `null`. Always save runtime files to `user://`!
debugChallenge.hint: Look at the virtual filesystem prefix (`res://` vs `user://`) passed to `FileAccess.open()`.
